products.name: Krea AI
products.note: Real-time video generation; creative tool; content moderation; emerging platform

reading.body:
Krea aggregates third-party video and image generation models from ByteDance, Google, Minimax, and Alibaba into a single creative interface, rather than building its own foundation models.

The platform's strategy is access, not infrastructure. Users can generate real-time video at resolutions up to 2K and images at 4K through models they could not reach individually. Krea surfaces Seedance variants from ByteDance, Veo and Gemini models from Google, Minimax's frontier video model, and Alibaba's video capabilities alongside web search and code execution tools for specialized tasks like rendering charts and QR codes. This is an aggregation play in a field increasingly defined by model proliferation.

For AI deployment, this matters because it shows the shift from monolithic platforms to composable ones. Users no longer choose a single vendor's video model. They choose an interface that routes requests to whichever model fits the task. The compute cost moves downstream to the model providers, while Krea absorbs infrastructure costs for serving inference at real-time latency. Whether real-time video generation at scale strains the grid depends on user volume and inference frequency, neither of which this data covers.

The data does not include Krea's funding, user count, compute infrastructure location, or power consumption. It does not explain why these particular models were selected or how their inference loads are distributed. It records what Krea offers, not what it costs to run.

profile_text.body:
Krea describes itself as a creative AI suite for generating, editing, and enhancing images and videos, and says it can be used for free. Its website lists a large catalog of third-party and in-house generative models spanning video, image, and audio, including ByteDance's Seedance and Seedream lines, Google's Gemini video and flash image models, Alibaba's Qwen video and image models, Black Forest Labs' video editing model, and FLUX 3, which the site says renders up to 20 seconds in a single pass with multilingual speech, effects, and ambience. The site also lists Muse Image, which it says plans before rendering by searching the web and running code, and describes several models by their reference-image, resolution, and clip-length limits.

The company's tracked product is Krea AI, listed under video generation and editing, with notes describing real-time video generation, content moderation, and an emerging platform. Krea is recorded as headquartered in San Francisco.

No lawsuits, MCP servers, or other filings are recorded for the company.
